claim: Skeletal muscle maintenance depends on motor innervation at neuromuscular junctions (NMJs).
source: Skeletal muscle maintenance depends on motor innervation at neuromuscular junctions (NMJs).
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about skeletal muscle biology.

claim: Satellite cells are deemed to have little impact on NMJ repair and maintenance processes.
source: Multiple mechanisms contribute to NMJ repair and maintenance; however muscle stem cells (satellite cells, SCs), are deemed to have little impact on these processes.
evidence: This reflects the prevailing view in the field prior to this study, based on existing literature.

claim: SC depletion exacerbated muscle atrophy connected to neuromuscular disruption.
source: We found SC depletion exacerbated muscle atrophy and type transitions connected to neuromuscular disruption.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SC depletion exacerbated myofiber type transitions connected to neuromuscular disruption.
source: We found SC depletion exacerbated muscle atrophy and type transitions connected to neuromuscular disruption.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Elevated fibrosis was specific to SC depletion and neuromuscular disruption.
source: Also, elevated fibrosis and further declines in force generation were specific to SC depletion and neuromuscular disruption.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Further declines in force generation were specific to SC depletion and neuromuscular disruption.
source: Also, elevated fibrosis and further declines in force generation were specific to SC depletion and neuromuscular disruption.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Fate analysis revealed SC activity near regenerating NMJs.
source: Fate analysis revealed SC activity near regenerating NMJs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data using lineage tracing.

claim: SC depletion aggravated deficits in reinnervation at regenerating NMJs.
source: Moreover, SC depletion aggravated deficits in reinnervation and post-synaptic morphology at regenerating NMJs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SC depletion aggravated deficits in post-synaptic morphology at regenerating NMJs.
source: Moreover, SC depletion aggravated deficits in reinnervation and post-synaptic morphology at regenerating NMJs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Adult skeletal muscle possesses a remarkable capacity for regeneration.
source: Although primarily a post-mitotic tissue, adult skeletal muscle possesses a remarkable capacity for regeneration.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about skeletal muscle biology.

claim: Adult skeletal muscle regeneration capacity is endowed by satellite cells identified by Pax7 expression.
source: This capacity is endowed by a population of resident stem cells, satellite cells (SCs), identified by the expression of the paired box transcription factor Pax7 (Tajbakhsh, 2009; Brack and Rando, 2012; Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In adults, SCs normally reside in a quiescent state at the interface between the myofiber and overlying basal lamina.
source: In adults, SCs normally reside in a quiescent state at the interface between the myofiber and overlying basal lamina (Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: In response to degenerative stimuli, Pax7+ SCs activate and divide to produce myogenic progenitors for skeletal muscle regeneration.
source: However, in response to degenerative stimuli, Pax7+ SCs activate and divide to produce myogenic progenitors for skeletal muscle regeneration (Tajbakhsh, 2009; Yin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Depletion of Pax7+ SCs has shown these cells to be an essential source of myonuclei for skeletal muscle regeneration.
source: Both depletion of Pax7+ SCs and targeted disruption of Pax7 have shown these cells to be an essential source of myonuclei for skeletal muscle regeneration (Relaix and Zammit, 2012; Gunther et al., 2013; von Maltzahn et al., 2013; Lepper et al., 2011; Murphy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Targeted disruption of Pax7 has shown these cells to be an essential source of myonuclei for skeletal muscle regeneration.
source: Both depletion of Pax7+ SCs and targeted disruption of Pax7 have shown these cells to be an essential source of myonuclei for skeletal muscle regeneration (Relaix and Zammit, 2012; Gunther et al., 2013; von Maltzahn et al., 2013; Lepper et al., 2011; Murphy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Depletion studies have revealed roles for Pax7+ SCs in late stages of experimentally induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy.
source: Depletion studies have revealed roles for Pax7+ SCs in late stages of experimentally induced skeletal muscle hypertrophy (Fry et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: SCs were shown to function as a source of growth factors to facilitate bone fracture healing.
source: Recently, SCs were also shown to function as a source of growth factors to facilitate bone fracture healing (Abou-Khalil et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: SCs contribute to myofibers during aging.
source: Similar strategies have shown SCs contribute to myofibers and regulate aspects of skeletal muscle integrity during aging (Fry et al., 2015; Keefe et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SCs regulate aspects of skeletal muscle integrity during aging.
source: Similar strategies have shown SCs contribute to myofibers and regulate aspects of skeletal muscle integrity during aging (Fry et al., 2015; Keefe et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In adults, each myofiber is innervated by a single axon from a motor neuron.
source: In adults, each myofiber is innervated by a single axon from a motor neuron (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Innervation occurs at a specialized site in the central region of myofibers, the neuromuscular junction (NMJ).
source: Innervation occurs at a specialized site in the central region of myofibers, the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The NMJ occupies approximately 0.1% of the surface area of a myofiber.
source: The NMJ, which occupies approximately 0.1% of the surface area of a myofiber, initiates action potential propagation required for excitation/contraction coupling to generate force for movement and maintain myofiber properties (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999; Bassel-Duby and Olson, 2006; Wu et al., 2010; Schiaffino and Reggiani, 2011).
evidence: This is a quantitative fact supported by citations.

claim: The NMJ initiates action potential propagation required for excitation/contraction coupling to generate force for movement and maintain myofiber properties.
source: The NMJ, which occupies approximately 0.1% of the surface area of a myofiber, initiates action potential propagation required for excitation/contraction coupling to generate force for movement and maintain myofiber properties (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999; Bassel-Duby and Olson, 2006; Wu et al., 2010; Schiaffino and Reggiani, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Neuromuscular disruptions elicit severe myofiber atrophy.
source: Consistent with a vital role for NMJ integrity in skeletal muscle maintenance, neuromuscular disruptions elicit severe myofiber atrophy, and are frequently associated with skeletal muscle dysfunction observed in the context of neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) and aging (Murray et al., 2010; Gonzalez-Freire et al., 2014; Moloney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Neuromuscular disruptions are frequently associated with skeletal muscle dysfunction observed in the context of neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) and aging.
source: Consistent with a vital role for NMJ integrity in skeletal muscle maintenance, neuromuscular disruptions elicit severe myofiber atrophy, and are frequently associated with skeletal muscle dysfunction observed in the context of neuromuscular diseases (NMDs) and aging (Murray et al., 2010; Gonzalez-Freire et al., 2014; Moloney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The regeneration of NMJs in response to peripheral nerve lesions can occur.
source: The regeneration of NMJs in response to peripheral nerve lesions can occur, however the length and quality of recovery depends on the severity of injury (Buti et al., 1996; Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The length and quality of NMJ recovery depends on the severity of injury.
source: The regeneration of NMJs in response to peripheral nerve lesions can occur, however the length and quality of recovery depends on the severity of injury (Buti et al., 1996; Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The initial reinnervation of synaptic basal lamina by motor axons can proceed in the absence of myofibers.
source: Remarkably, the initial reinnervation of synaptic basal lamina by motor axons can proceed in the absence of myofibers (Sanes et al., 1978; Sanes and Lichtman, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the absence of myofibers and associated SCs, the continued maintenance of reinnervated NMJs on basal lamina ghosts eventually declines.
source: However, in the absence of myofibers and associated SCs, the continued maintenance of reinnervated NMJs on basal lamina ghosts eventually declines (Sanes et al., 1978; Sanes and Lichtman, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Myofiber derived factors or associated SCs may be required for the continued differentiation and maintenance of regenerated NMJs.
source: These observations indicate that myofiber derived factors or associated SCs may be required for the continued differentiation and maintenance of regenerated NMJs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observations cited in the previous sentence.

claim: Myofiber components and derived factors have been identified to assist in the progressive differentiation of developing and regenerating NMJs.
source: Accordingly, myofiber components and derived factors have been identified to assist in the progressive differentiation of developing and regenerating NMJs (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999; Fox et al., 2007; Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In models of chronic denervation where reinnervation is prevented, SCs activate and divide.
source: In models of chronic denervation, where reinnervation is prevented, SCs activate and divide; however, the derived progenitors migrate into interstitial spaces, undergo defective differentiation or are lost via apoptosis (Dedkov et al., 2001; Borisov et al., 2005; Bruusgaard and Gundersen, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In models of chronic denervation, SC-derived progenitors migrate into interstitial spaces, undergo defective differentiation or are lost via apoptosis.
source: In models of chronic denervation, where reinnervation is prevented, SCs activate and divide; however, the derived progenitors migrate into interstitial spaces, undergo defective differentiation or are lost via apoptosis (Dedkov et al., 2001; Borisov et al., 2005; Bruusgaard and Gundersen, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Little turnover of myonuclei has been observed in chronically denervated myofibers.
source: Furthermore, little turnover of myonuclei and fusion of myogenic progenitors to chronically denervated parent myofibers have been observed (Bruusgaard and Gundersen, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Little fusion of myogenic progenitors to chronically denervated parent myofibers has been observed.
source: Furthermore, little turnover of myonuclei and fusion of myogenic progenitors to chronically denervated parent myofibers have been observed (Bruusgaard and Gundersen, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Studies have suggested SCs have limited, if any, roles in the regeneration of NMJs upon neuromuscular disruptions.
source: Collectively, these studies have suggested SCs have limited, if any, roles in the regeneration of NMJs upon neuromuscular disruptions (Gundersen and Bruusgaard, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: A modest albeit significant increase in Pax7+ SC number was observed 6 weeks after SNT surgery.
source: Consistent with previous reports, a modest albeit significant increase in Pax7+ SC number was observed 6 weeks after SNT surgery (Figure 1) (Snow, 1983; Viguie et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1 and citations to previous literature.

claim: After Tmx administration, extensive depletion of Pax7+ SCs occurred regardless of sham or SNT surgery.
source: After Tmx administration, extensive depletion of Pax7+ SCs occurred regardless of sham or SNT surgery (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: SC depletion did not induce further loss of muscle mass after SNT.
source: While the mass of TA, extensor digitorum longus (EDL) and soleus muscles 6 weeks after SNT relative to contralateral sham controls remained low, SC depletion did not induce further loss of muscle mass (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Only modest reductions in myonuclear density occurred after SNT and SC depletion in EDL muscles.
source: Examination of individual myofibers from EDL muscles that had been fixed prior to isolation from lower limbs revealed only modest reductions in myonuclear density after SNT and SC depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and C.

claim: A small albeit significant level of myonuclear turnover was observed in P7DTA sham muscles.
source: Based on these moderate losses, a small albeit significant level of myonuclear turnover was observed in P7DTA sham muscles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the myonuclear density data.

claim: The magnitude of myonuclear loss after SNT relative to sham in P7DTA skeletal muscles is small.
source: Therefore, the magnitude of myonuclear loss after SNT relative to sham in P7DTA skeletal muscles is small (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Ctrl myofiber size after SNT remained ~25% lower relative to contralateral sham despite 6 weeks of recovery.
source: Despite 6 weeks of recovery, Ctrl myofiber size after SNT remained ∼25% lower relative to contralateral sham, however, SC depletion led to further SNT-induced myofiber atrophy (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: SC depletion led to further SNT-induced myofiber atrophy.
source: Despite 6 weeks of recovery, Ctrl myofiber size after SNT remained ∼25% lower relative to contralateral sham, however, SC depletion led to further SNT-induced myofiber atrophy (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: A significant shift towards smaller myofiber sizes after SNT surgery was observed upon SC depletion.
source: Distribution analysis of myofiber size did not reveal any significant differences between Ctrl and P7DTA muscles after sham surgery, but a significant shift towards smaller sizes after SNT surgery was observed upon SC depletion (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: No change in myofiber numbers was observed after SNT and SC depletion.
source: No change in myofiber numbers was observed after SNT and SC depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SNT surgery alone did not increase MCT content.
source: Surprisingly, although SNT surgery alone did not increase MCT content, when combined with SC depletion, a significant increase in fibrosis was observed (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: When SNT was combined with SC depletion, a significant increase in fibrosis was observed.
source: Surprisingly, although SNT surgery alone did not increase MCT content, when combined with SC depletion, a significant increase in fibrosis was observed (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The lack of change in the mass of SC-depleted skeletal muscles relative to Ctrl after SNT surgery was accompanied by both increased fibrosis and myofiber atrophy.
source: Therefore, the lack of change in the mass of SC-depleted skeletal muscles relative to Ctrl after SNT surgery was accompanied by both increased fibrosis and myofiber atrophy.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined observations of muscle mass, fibrosis, and myofiber size data.

claim: Type I myofibers are characterized by slower contraction kinetics and lower force generation.
source: In this regard, type I fibers are characterized by slower contraction kinetics and lower force generation, whereas at the other end of the continuum type IIB fibers exhibit faster contraction kinetics and greater force generation (Mantilla and Sieck, 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Type IIB myofibers exhibit faster contraction kinetics and greater force generation.
source: In this regard, type I fibers are characterized by slower contraction kinetics and lower force generation, whereas at the other end of the continuum type IIB fibers exhibit faster contraction kinetics and greater force generation (Mantilla and Sieck, 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Myofibers innervated by the same motor neuron primarily express one MyHC isoform.
source: Consistent with the vital influence of neural activity on myofiber type, myofibers innervated by the same motor neuron primarily express one MyHC isoform, and cross-innervation can induce the expression of isoforms indicative of the foreign nerve (Murray et al., 2010; Moloney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cross-innervation can induce the expression of MyHC isoforms indicative of the foreign nerve.
source: Consistent with the vital influence of neural activity on myofiber type, myofibers innervated by the same motor neuron primarily express one MyHC isoform, and cross-innervation can induce the expression of isoforms indicative of the foreign nerve (Murray et al., 2010; Moloney et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Neuromuscular disruption is frequently associated with abnormal profiles of MyHC isoform expression within a given skeletal muscle.
source: Neuromuscular disruption is frequently associated with abnormal profiles of MyHC isoform expression within a given skeletal muscle (Klitgaard et al., 1990; Krivickas et al., 2002; Palencia et al., 2005; Stevens et al., 2008; Schiaffino and Reggiani, 2011; Rowan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A typical feature of NMD and aging skeletal muscle is an increased occurrence of hybrid myofibers whereby two or more MyHC isoforms are co-expressed.
source: A typical feature of NMD and aging skeletal muscle is an increased occurrence of hybrid myofibers whereby two or more MyHC isoforms are co-expressed (Klitgaard et al., 1990; Krivickas et al., 2002; Palencia et al., 2005; Stevens et al., 2008; Rowan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Very few MyHC IIX hybrid myofibers were found in adult inner TA/EDL muscles after sham surgery regardless of genotype.
source: Very few MyHC IIX hybrid myofibers were found in adult inner TA/EDL muscles after sham surgery regardless of genotype (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Elevations in the proportion of hybrid myofibers were observed in Ctrl inner TA/EDL muscles 6 weeks after SNT.
source: Elevations in the proportion of hybrid myofibers were observed in Ctrl inner TA/EDL muscles 6 weeks after SNT, a phenotype exacerbated by SC depletion (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The elevation in hybrid myofibers after SNT was exacerbated by SC depletion.
source: Elevations in the proportion of hybrid myofibers were observed in Ctrl inner TA/EDL muscles 6 weeks after SNT, a phenotype exacerbated by SC depletion (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Very little if any expression of MyHC I was observed in inner TA/EDL muscles after SNT.
source: Assessment of inner TA/EDL muscles after SNT with antibodies specific for MyHC I, MyHC IIA and MyHC IIB revealed: i) very little if any expression of MyHC I; ii) inductions of MyHC IIA that were aggravated upon SC depletion; and iii) loss of MyHC IIB (Figure 4A and C–E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and C-E.

claim: Inductions of MyHC IIA after SNT were aggravated upon SC depletion.
source: Assessment of inner TA/EDL muscles after SNT with antibodies specific for MyHC I, MyHC IIA and MyHC IIB revealed: i) very little if any expression of MyHC I; ii) inductions of MyHC IIA that were aggravated upon SC depletion; and iii) loss of MyHC IIB (Figure 4A and C–E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and C-E.

claim: Loss of MyHC IIB was observed after SNT.
source: Assessment of inner TA/EDL muscles after SNT with antibodies specific for MyHC I, MyHC IIA and MyHC IIB revealed: i) very little if any expression of MyHC I; ii) inductions of MyHC IIA that were aggravated upon SC depletion; and iii) loss of MyHC IIB (Figure 4A and C–E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and C-E.

claim: The majority of hybrid myofibers observed after SNT are presumably type IIA/IIX.
source: Together, these data indicate that the majority of hybrid myofibers observed after SNT are presumably type IIA/IIX.
evidence: This is an inference based on the MyHC expression data.

claim: A similar lengthening in time to peak tension (TTP) was observed in Ctrl and P7DTA EDL muscles after SNT.
source: A similar lengthening in time to peak tension (TTP) was observed in Ctrl and P7DTA EDL muscles after SNT (Figure 5A, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Lengthening of TTP 6 weeks after SNT is consistent with shifts in MyHC expression with slower contractile character.
source: Although lengthening of TTP 6 weeks after SNT is consistent with shifts in MyHC expression with slower contractile character, SC depletion did not further influence this property.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the TTP data with the MyHC expression data.

claim: SC depletion did not further influence time to peak tension after SNT.
source: Although lengthening of TTP 6 weeks after SNT is consistent with shifts in MyHC expression with slower contractile character, SC depletion did not further influence this property.
evidence: This is supported by the TTP data.

claim: Significant deficits in peak absolute force generation were found in P7DTA EDL muscles in comparison to Ctrl after SNT at progressively higher frequencies.
source: We found significant deficits in peak absolute and specific force generation in P7DTA EDL muscles in comparison to Ctrl after SNT at progressively higher frequencies (Figure 5B,C, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5B,C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Significant deficits in peak specific force generation were found in P7DTA EDL muscles in comparison to Ctrl after SNT at progressively higher frequencies.
source: We found significant deficits in peak absolute and specific force generation in P7DTA EDL muscles in comparison to Ctrl after SNT at progressively higher frequencies (Figure 5B,C, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5B,C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The exacerbated deficits in skeletal muscle integrity upon SC depletion and SNT were accompanied by declines in whole skeletal muscle force generation.
source: Therefore, the exacerbated deficits in skeletal muscle integrity such as myofiber atrophy, increased MCT content and abnormal profiles of MyHC expression upon SC depletion and SNT were accompanied by declines in whole skeletal muscle force generation.
evidence: This is an inference connecting multiple observations about muscle integrity and force generation.

claim: Only a fraction (~25%) of the SC pool in TA muscles had incorporated BrdU after SNT.
source: Consistent with limited SC activation, only a fraction (∼25%) of the SC pool in TA muscles had incorporated BrdU after SNT (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: 24 hr after the last Tmx administration, >90% of the SC pool was GFP+ in P7mTmG mice.
source: We found that 24 hr after the last Tmx administration, >90% of the SC pool was GFP+, whereas myofibers were devoid of GFP label (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: 24 hr after the last Tmx administration, myofibers were devoid of GFP label in P7mTmG mice.
source: We found that 24 hr after the last Tmx administration, >90% of the SC pool was GFP+, whereas myofibers were devoid of GFP label (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: A marked increase in GFP+ myofibers was observed in transverse sections from the mid belly of TA and EDL muscles after SNT in comparison to sham.
source: In comparison to sham, a marked increase in GFP + myofibers was observed in transverse sections from the mid belly of TA and EDL muscles after SNT (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: A high proportion of myofibers within TA and EDL muscles have undergone a fusion event after SNT.
source: Although these data indicate a high proportion of myofibers within TA and EDL muscles have undergone a fusion event after SNT, this activity likely reflects limited fusion within a given myofiber consistent with modest losses of myonuclei within P7DTA myofibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the GFP+ myofiber data and myonuclear loss data.

claim: The fusion activity after SNT likely reflects limited fusion within a given myofiber consistent with modest losses of myonuclei within P7DTA myofibers.
source: Although these data indicate a high proportion of myofibers within TA and EDL muscles have undergone a fusion event after SNT, this activity likely reflects limited fusion within a given myofiber consistent with modest losses of myonuclei within P7DTA myofibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the GFP+ myofiber data and myonuclear loss data.

claim: The occurrence of central nucleated myofibers (CNF) was minimal after SNT.
source: The occurrence of central nucleated myofibers (CNF), an indicator of degenerative/regenerative events of myofibers, was minimal and cannot explain the observed induction of GFP + myofibers after SNT (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The occurrence of CNF cannot explain the observed induction of GFP+ myofibers after SNT.
source: The occurrence of central nucleated myofibers (CNF), an indicator of degenerative/regenerative events of myofibers, was minimal and cannot explain the observed induction of GFP + myofibers after SNT (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the CNF and GFP+ myofiber data.

claim: After sham surgery, only a small fraction of myofibers were GFP positive.
source: After sham surgery, only a small fraction of myofibers were GFP positive; none of these fibers had GFP throughout, and most labels were found either at the ends or middle regions, the latter being where NMJs are located (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: After sham surgery, none of the GFP positive myofibers had GFP throughout.
source: After sham surgery, only a small fraction of myofibers were GFP positive; none of these fibers had GFP throughout, and most labels were found either at the ends or middle regions, the latter being where NMJs are located (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: After sham surgery, most GFP labels in myofibers were found either at the ends or middle regions where NMJs are located.
source: After sham surgery, only a small fraction of myofibers were GFP positive; none of these fibers had GFP throughout, and most labels were found either at the ends or middle regions, the latter being where NMJs are located (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: After SNT surgery a greater proportion of myofibers were GFP positive, indicating the activation of at least some SCs and fusion of SC derived progenitors to myofibers.
source: After SNT surgery a greater proportion of myofibers were GFP positive, indicating the activation of at least some SCs and fusion of SC derived progenitors to myofibers (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7E and is an inference from the GFP labeling.

claim: The majority of the GFP label found in myofibers isolated from EDL muscles after SNT was located in the middle, within the vicinity of NMJs.
source: In addition, the majority of the GFP label found in myofibers isolated from EDL muscles after SNT was located in the middle, within the vicinity of NMJs (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Neuromuscular disruption led to regional SC derived contributions along the length of a myofiber in proximity to the NMJ.
source: Therefore, neuromuscular disruption led to regional SC derived contributions along the length of a myofiber in proximity to the NMJ.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GFP labeling pattern data.

claim: A large increase in partially/fully denervated NMJs in Ctrl TA muscles was observed after SNT compared to sham surgery.
source: Consistent with previous reports, a large increase in partially/fully denervated NMJs in Ctrl TA muscles was observed after SNT compared to sham surgery, suggesting incomplete regeneration of NMJs (Figure 8B) (Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8B and citation to previous literature.

claim: The increase in partially/fully denervated NMJs after SNT suggests incomplete regeneration of NMJs.
source: Consistent with previous reports, a large increase in partially/fully denervated NMJs in Ctrl TA muscles was observed after SNT compared to sham surgery, suggesting incomplete regeneration of NMJs (Figure 8B) (Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an inference based on the denervation data.

claim: SC depletion was associated with a significantly higher proportion of NMJs that remained partially/fully denervated 6 weeks after SNT surgery.
source: Examination of P7DTA NMJs revealed that SC depletion was associated with a significantly higher proportion of NMJs that remained partially/fully denervated 6 weeks after SNT surgery (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Post-natal NMJ maturation is associated with post-synaptic morphological transitions from a plaque-like to a pretzel-like shape due to the formation of post-synaptic membrane invaginations (junctional folds).
source: Post-natal NMJ maturation is associated with post-synaptic morphological transitions from a plaque-like to a pretzel-like shape due to the formation of post-synaptic membrane invaginations (junctional folds) (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Aged and NMD-afflicted skeletal muscles are frequently associated with NMJ degeneration, manifested by loss of elaborate AChR-enriched branches and the characteristic pretzel-like morphology of mature adult NMJs.
source: Aged and NMD-afflicted skeletal muscles are frequently associated with NMJ degeneration, manifested by loss of elaborate AChR-enriched branches and the characteristic pretzel-like morphology of mature adult NMJs (Valdez et al., 2010, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Very few degenerated NMJs were found in Ctrl or P7DTA TA muscles 6 weeks after sham surgery regardless of genotype.
source: Very few degenerated NMJs were found in Ctrl or P7DTA TA muscles 6 weeks after sham surgery regardless of genotype (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: After SNT surgery there was a marked increase in the proportion of degenerated NMJs.
source: After SNT surgery there was a marked increase in the proportion of degenerated NMJs, a percentage that was substantially elevated by ∼ 25% with SC depletion (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The proportion of degenerated NMJs after SNT was substantially elevated by ~25% with SC depletion.
source: After SNT surgery there was a marked increase in the proportion of degenerated NMJs, a percentage that was substantially elevated by ∼ 25% with SC depletion (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Post-synaptic myonuclei are enriched at most adult NMJs.
source: Enriched at most adult NMJs are clusters of post-synaptic myonuclei specialized for the expression of genes required for AChR consolidation and the differentiation of pre-synaptic nerve terminals (Sanes and Lichtman, 1999; Hippenmeyer et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2007; Mejat et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Post-synaptic myonuclei are specialized for the expression of genes required for AChR consolidation and the differentiation of pre-synaptic nerve terminals.
